info.name: KarSathi — 8-Week MVP Test Suite
info.description:
End-to-end test collection for KarSathi WhatsApp CFO assistant for Indian MSMEs.
Covers all 4 build fortnights: onboarding, invoice parsing, GST risk, and hardening.

All /webhook requests use exact Meta WhatsApp Cloud API payload format.
All /filings and /filing-confirmation requests use the agreed CTO ↔ CF-B JSON contract.

Realistic data: Sharma Kirana Store, Jaipur, Rajasthan | GSTIN: 08ABCCS1234F1Z1 | Turnover: under ₹40L

item.name: Weeks 1–2 — WhatsApp Bot + Business Profiling
item.description: Set up WhatsApp webhook, onboard Ramesh Sharma (Sharma Kirana Store, Jaipur, Rajasthan), parse Udyam certificate, and return compliance profile with applicable laws.

item.name: GET /health — Server health check

request.description: Verify the FastAPI server is running and all dependencies (PostgreSQL, Redis) are reachable.

item.name: POST /webhook — User sends 'Hi', bot starts onboarding

request.description: Simulates a new user sending 'Hi' on WhatsApp. The bot should detect a new user (no profile in DB), send a welcome message in Hindi + English, and begin the 3-question onboarding flow via WhatsApp button templates.

exec: pm.test('Onboarding started flag is true', function () {
pm.test('WhatsApp message was sent to user', function () {
pm.test('Next question field is present', function () {

item.name: POST /webhook — User answers 3 onboarding questions (kirana / Rajasthan / under 40L)

request.description: Simulates the user completing the 3-question onboarding flow via WhatsApp Flows (nfm_reply). Answers: segment=kirana, state=Rajasthan, turnover=under_40L. The bot should create a profile in PostgreSQL and run the Knowledge Graph to return a compliance summary.

exec: pm.test('Compliance summary was sent to user', function () {
pm.test('Profile contains correct turnover band', function () {

item.name: POST /webhook — User forwards Udyam certificate image

request.description: User forwards their Udyam certificate image. The bot should: (1) download the media via Meta API, (2) pass to Claude vision for extraction, (3) extract GSTIN, Udyam number, business type, state, turnover, (4) update the user profile in PostgreSQL, (5) confirm extraction to user in Hindi.

exec: pm.test('Document parsed flag is true', function () {

item.name: GET /compliance-profile/{wa_id} — Returns applicable laws for user profile

request.description: Queries the Knowledge Graph for all applicable laws given the user's profile (kirana, Rajasthan, under 40L). Returns the compliance obligations, risk score, and filing deadlines. This is the output the bot sends to the MSME owner after onboarding.

exec: pm.test('GST is in applicable laws', function () {
pm.test('MSMED is in applicable laws', function () {
pm.test('RJ S&E Act is in applicable laws (Rajasthan state law)', function () {
pm.test('FSSAI is in applicable laws (food/kirana)', function () {
pm.test('risk_score_inr is a non-negative number', function () {

item.name: Weeks 3–4 — Invoice Parser + Form I Risk Engine
item.description: Parse invoice photos and bank SMS, build vendor aging, calculate Form I overdue amounts with penalty risk and Section 43B(h) tax deduction loss. Finalize the CTO → CF-B JSON contract.

item.name: POST /webhook — User forwards invoice photo

request.description: User forwards an invoice photo from Gupta Wholesale Traders (a registered MSME vendor). Claude vision extracts: vendor_name, GSTIN, amount, invoice_date. The Udyam lookup flags this as an MSME vendor. The invoice is stored with is_msme_vendor=true and days_outstanding calculated.

exec: pm.test('Invoice parsed flag is true', function () {

item.name: POST /webhook — User forwards bank SMS text

request.description: User forwards an HDFC Bank debit SMS. Regex parser extracts: amount=18500, payee=Mehta Traders Pvt Ltd, date=28-Jun-26, reference=402613855921. The bot matches this payment to an outstanding invoice if one exists, marks it as paid, and recalculates Form I exposure.

exec: pm.test('Payment recorded flag is true', function () {
pm.test('SMS parsed as bank transaction', function () {

item.name: GET /invoices/{wa_id} — All parsed invoices for user

request.description: Returns all invoices stored for Ramesh Sharma's account, including those parsed from photos, PDFs, and bank SMS. Each invoice shows MSME vendor flag, days outstanding, and Form I relevance.

exec: pm.test('Each invoice has required fields', function () {
pm.test('No invoice has negative amount', function () {

item.name: GET /form1-assessment/{wa_id} — Form I overdue amounts, penalty risk, 43B(h) tax loss

request.description: Runs the Form I risk engine for the current assessment period. Sums all overdue amounts to MSME-registered vendors past 45 days, calculates MCA penalty using the compound interest formula, and links Section 43B(h) tax deduction loss at the user's estimated tax slab.

exec: pm.test('Total overdue INR is non-negative', function () {
pm.test('Penalty risk INR is non-negative', function () {
pm.test('Tax deduction loss INR present', function () {

item.name: POST /filings — CTO sends filing request to CF-B pipeline (JSON contract)

request.description: The agreed JSON contract between CTO and CF-B. This payload is sent by the CTO's bot when a user triggers 'File Form I'. CF-B's filing pipeline consumes this to: (1) create a filing request record, (2) assign a CA, (3) pre-fill Form I fields, (4) add to CA dashboard queue. Breaking changes to this schema require sign-off from both owners.

exec: pm.test('Filing ID assigned by CF-B', function () {

item.name: Weeks 5–6 — GST Risk + Daily Intelligence Message
item.description: GST ITC reversal risk from unfiled vendor GSTR-1, daily 8am intelligence snapshot, upgrade prompt for free-tier users, and filing trigger flow for paid users.

item.name: GET /gst-itc-risk/{wa_id} — ITC at-risk from vendor GSTR-1 non-filing

request.description: For each purchase invoice where the vendor has not filed GSTR-1, the claimed ITC is at risk of reversal by the GST department. This endpoint calculates total ITC claimed vs. ITC at-risk, and returns a vendor-level breakdown. Note: for MVP, GSTR-1 status is directional (best-effort) — disclosed honestly to users.

exec: pm.test('ITC at-risk <= total ITC claimed', function () {
pm.test('Vendors not filed array present', function () {

item.name: GET /daily-snapshot/{wa_id} — Revenue, unpaid invoices, GST risk, Form I countdown, cash stuck

request.description: Builds the daily 8am intelligence message for the user. Aggregates 5 numbers from the DB: revenue from bank SMS, unpaid vendor invoices, GST ITC risk, days until Form I deadline, and cash stuck in overdue receivables. The n8n scheduler calls this at 8am IST and sends the result via WhatsApp template message.

exec: pm.test('Form I days remaining present', function () {

item.name: POST /webhook — Paid user sends 'File Form I', bot starts data collection

request.description: Paid user triggers the filing flow by sending 'File Form I'. The bot checks user.plan == 'paid', starts the structured data collection conversation, pre-fills any fields already extracted from invoices, asks for missing fields only, and prepares the filing request payload for CF-B.

exec: pm.test('Filing flow started flag is true', function () {
pm.test('Flow type is Form I', function () {
pm.test('Next question sent to user', function () {
pm.test('Session state saved to Redis', function () {

item.name: POST /upgrade-prompt/{wa_id} — Trigger upgrade button message

request.description: Sends a WhatsApp button template message to a free-tier user prompting them to upgrade to ₹499/month. The button links to the Razorpay payment page (manual link for MVP). Triggered when the user sees their Form I risk number and the bot surfaces the 'Remove this risk' CTA.

exec: pm.test('WhatsApp message sent to user', function () {
pm.test('Button type is payment link', function () {

item.name: Weeks 7–8 — Hardening + Beta
item.description: Edge case handling (blurry invoices, offline resume), admin monitoring view, rule engine audit log, and CF-B's MCA confirmation webhook closing the loop back to the user.

item.name: POST /webhook — Blurry invoice photo (fallback: 'please type the amount')

request.description: Tests the parser fallback for unreadable invoice images (blurry, dark, rotated, handwritten). The bot should NOT return an error to the user. It should gracefully fall back and ask the user to type the amount manually. This is a critical UX path — a bad error message here causes churn.

exec: pm.test('Fallback triggered flag is true', function () {
pm.test('Fallback message sent to user in plain English', function () {
pm.test('Fallback message text contains expected phrase', function () {
const hasExpectedPhrase = msg.includes('could not read') || msg.includes('please type') || msg.includes('amount') || msg.includes('parhne mein');
pm.test('No SQL/tech error exposed to user', function () {

item.name: POST /webhook — User resumes mid-flow conversation after going offline

request.description: User went offline mid-flow (e.g., after receiving the blurry invoice fallback prompt asking them to type the amount). They return the next day and type '48500'. The bot must retrieve conversation context from Redis, understand this is an amount response in the invoice entry flow, and continue from where they left off. Tests conversation state management.

exec: pm.test('Flow resumed flag is true', function () {
pm.test('Next step in flow present', function () {

request.description: Internal admin view for the CTO. Returns all registered users with their business profiles, current risk scores, and filing statuses. Used for monitoring beta users and identifying issues. Requires X-Admin-Key header — must return 401 if key is missing or wrong.

exec: pm.test('Each user has required fields', function () {
pm.test('Ramesh Sharma is in the list', function () {

item.name: GET /audit-log/{wa_id} — Rule engine evaluation log for user

request.description: Returns the full rule engine evaluation log for a user. Every time the Knowledge Graph processes a message, the input values, rules evaluated, and output result are logged. This is the audit trail that proves the bot's compliance advice is correct and deterministic — critical for trust and debugging.

exec: pm.test('Each entry has required fields', function () {
pm.test('Total evaluated rules count present', function () {

item.name: POST /filing-confirmation — CF-B sends MCA confirmation back to CTO webhook

request.description: CF-B sends this confirmation after the CA has successfully filed Form I with MCA and received the acknowledgement number. This closes the loop: the CTO backend receives the confirmation, marks the filing as complete in the DB, updates the user's risk score to zero for Form I, and sends the final WhatsApp message to the MSME owner: 'Form I filed. Penalty avoided: ₹12,000.'

pm.test('Filing marked as FILED in DB', function () {
pm.test('MCA confirmation number echoed back', function () {
pm.test('Penalty avoided amount in WhatsApp message', function () {
pm.test('User Form I risk score reset to zero', function () {
